'''Kazama Shrine''' (かざまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in the Kazama area of {{ill|Nagano (city)|en|Nagano (city)|qid=Q128849|lt=Nagano City|1=Nagano (city)}}, Nagano Prefecture.

The shrine is identified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki_Jinmyocho}}.

== Overview ==
The shrine is situated approximately 3 km southeast of {{ill|Nagano Station|en|Nagano Station|qid=Q374916|lt=Nagano Station|1=Nagano Station}}, in a residential area slightly off the prefectural road {{ill|Nagano Prefectural Road 34|ja|長野県道34号長野菅平線|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagano Prefectural Road 34|1=Nagano Prefectural Road Route 34|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11654596}}.

Records indicate that in {{ill|860 CE|ja|貞観2年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/860 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, "Hyoubetsu Shrine" was granted Rank in the court hierarchy. In {{ill|979 CE|ja|天元2年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/979 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Tadanobu Yajima, a minor branch of the {{ill|Suwa clan|en|Suwa clan|qid=Q2975376|lt=Suwa clan|1=Suwa clan}}, was dispatched as a steward and took the surname Kazama, marking the origins of various {{ill|Kazama clan|lt=Kazama clan|lt=Kazama clans|ja|風間氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kazama clans|qq=}}.

The shrine preserves a traditional lion dance known as the "Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance," which has been performed since {{ill|1822 CE|ja|文政5年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1822 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. The dance features male lions wielding swords and no lyrics. It was designated a {{ill|Nagano City Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja|長野市選択無形民俗文化財|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagano City Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in {{ill|1998|en|1998|qid=Q2089|lt=Heisei 10|1=1998}}.<ref>[http://bunkazai-nagano.jp/modules/dbsearch/page1166.html Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance] - Nagano City Cultural Heritage Database</ref>

== History ==
* {{ill|596 CE|ja|推古天皇5年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/596 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (August): Mentioned in the {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki|1=Nihon Shoki}}.
* {{ill|860 CE|ja|貞観2年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/860 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (February): Recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qid=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|1=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}.
* {{ill|979 CE|ja|天元2年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/979 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}: Tadanobu Yajima of the Suwa clan was dispatched as a steward and adopted the name Kazama.
* {{ill|1697 CE|ja|元禄10年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1697 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}: Renamed from Suwa Shrine to Kazama Daimyōjin.<ref>[http://weekly-nagano.main.jp/2012/01/127.html 127 Kazama Shrine: The Wind deity Renamed as a Shikinaisha] - Weekly Nagano</ref>
* {{ill|1822 CE|ja|文政5年|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/1822 CE|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (September): Renamed Kazama Shrine by the Yoshida clan, who served as shrine administrators.
* {{ill|1998|en|1998|qid=Q2089|lt=Heisei 10|1=1998}} (August 1): The Kazama Shrine Daidaikagura Lion Dance was designated as a Nagano City Selected Intangible Folk Cultural Property.

== Access ==
* From {{ill|Nagano Station|en|Nagano Station|qid=Q374916|lt=Nagano Station|1=Nagano Station}} (JR East and Nagano Electric Railway), take the Alpico Kōtsū (Kawanakajima Bus) Route 46 to the "Kazama" stop. The shrine is a 2-minute walk from the bus stop.
